entry.name: ZoomMin
entry.label: Smallest zoom the overview reaches (1.0 is native scale).

entry.name: ZoomStep
entry.label: Zoom factor per wheel notch.

entry.name: GridBase
entry.label: Minor grid spacing in canvas pixels.

entry.name: GridOctaveFactor
entry.label: Each coarser grid octave is this many times larger.

entry.name: GridOctaves
entry.label: Number of grid octaves drawn.

entry.name: TileImage
entry.label: Optional image tiled across the canvas at 1:1. Empty draws the grid.

entry.name: Backdrop
entry.label: What the plane draws beyond the monitor frames: "wallpaper" (the default) puts the desktop's own wallpaper on the plane - exactly on the desks, and as a blurred, dimmed continuation of it across the rest of the view, so the plane reads as the desktop dissolving into a haze rather than repeating - with the ground grid over it; "grid" is the plain grid on Background, with no wallpaper at all.

entry.name: BackdropDim
entry.label: How far the blurred backdrop wallpaper is dimmed toward Background: 0 leaves it as it is, 0.45 (the default) keeps the desks and the windows reading on top of it, 1 hides it. Always 0 while the canvas slides at 1:1, where the plane and the desktop have to look identical. The desks themselves are never dimmed.

entry.name: BackdropBlur
entry.label: How blurred the backdrop continuation of the wallpaper is, in pixels: 0 draws it sharp (which reads as the wallpaper repeating, since it does not move with the plane), 48 (the default) is a soft haze the desks read on top of, higher is softer. The wallpaper on the desks themselves is always exact.

entry.name: BorderActivate
entry.label: Screen edges and corners that open the canvas (written by the Screen Edges settings page). 0 top, 1 top-right, 2 right, 3 bottom-right, 4 bottom, 5 bottom-left, 6 left, 7 top-left.

entry.name: TouchBorderActivate
entry.label: Touch screen edges that open the canvas.

entry.name: BorderSlide
entry.label: With this on, a screen edge or corner push pans the plane one step toward the pushed side instead of opening the canvas - a slide at 1:1, a camera step in the open canvas - the way a scrolling desktop moves, so the edges are a route around the plane rather than a door in and out of it. The canvas still opens from the chord, the toolbar and the panel button; pushing an edge repeatedly while a slide runs chains more steps.

entry.name: HudPosition
entry.label: Where the toolbar sits on the primary display: Top, TopLeft, TopRight, Bottom, BottomLeft, BottomRight, Left, Right.

entry.name: HudShape
entry.label: Toolbar shape: auto (square in a corner, horizontal on the top or bottom edge, vertical on a side), or horizontal, vertical, square.

entry.name: OpenZoom
entry.label: View when the canvas opens: "1" (the default) stays at 1:1, so the open canvas looks like the desktop until you move; "fit" zooms to every window and frame; any other number is a zoom anchored at the screen centre.

entry.name: FullscreenZoom
entry.label: View when the canvas opens while a fullscreen window is active: "0.85" (the default) steps out around the screen so the open canvas is visible instead of being the fullscreen app, pixel for pixel, at 1:1; "1" keeps the ordinary opening; "fit" zooms to everything. The chord and the canvas modifier both use it.

entry.name: BorderZoom
entry.label: View when a screen edge or corner opens the canvas: "0.8" (the default) steps out around the screen that was pushed, so the push shows the desks around it rather than the desktop it was on; "fit" shows every window and frame; "1" opens at 1:1 like any other opening. Anchored at that screen's centre, so the point an edge push leaves under the centre is the point applying comes back to. The chord and the toolbar still open at OpenZoom.

entry.name: KeyApply
entry.label: Keys that apply and close, as Qt key names without the Key_ prefix, comma separated. With a window selected they enter it focused; otherwise they enter the location under the screen centre.

entry.name: KeyHome
entry.label: Look through the current activity's frames.

entry.name: KeyOrigin
entry.label: Camera to the canvas origin.

entry.name: KeyFit
entry.label: Keys that zoom to fit, as Qt key names. F by default; W is taken by the pan-up key.

entry.name: KeyPan
entry.label: Held while dragging to pan from anywhere.

entry.name: KeyPanLeft
entry.label: In the open canvas, the key that pans the camera one step left (with the pass-through plugin loaded, keys go to the focused window and these do not apply).

entry.name: KeyPanRight
entry.label: In the open canvas, the key that pans the camera one step right.

entry.name: KeyPanUp
entry.label: In the open canvas, the key that pans the camera one step up.

entry.name: KeyPanDown
entry.label: In the open canvas, the key that pans the camera one step down.

entry.name: KeyNext
entry.label: In the open canvas, the key that steps the selection through the windows, the camera following to keep the chosen window in view.

entry.name: KeyPrev
entry.label: In the open canvas, the key that steps the selection through the windows the other way.

entry.name: PanHold
entry.label: Mouse buttons that navigate the open canvas while held down: any of LeftButton, MiddleButton, RightButton, BackButton, ForwardButton, comma separated. A held button is a portal into the canvas: wherever the pointer is, a drag on the ground pans and a drag on a window moves it on the plane, and the app under a window never sees the press. The middle button always navigates, whether or not it is listed here; empty by default, since the canvas hold below covers it.

entry.name: HoldDelay
entry.label: How long the canvas modifier must stay down before it opens the canvas, in milliseconds. Quicker presses pass through as the window's own clicks, so a game button bound to the same mouse button keeps working; raise this if a fast game click still opens the canvas.

entry.name: HoverDelay
entry.label: How long the pointer must rest on a window in the open canvas before input passes through to it, in milliseconds. A quicker pass-over stays the canvas's, so sweeping across the overworld never activates a window by accident; only a deliberate pause hands the pointer over. Raise this if windows still engage while you are just looking.

entry.name: WheelDoor
entry.label: The zoom door: with the canvas closed, the wheel over the bare ground zooms the world out of the location - the canvas opens at the 1:1 seam and the wheel keeps zooming into the overworld; zooming back in to 1:1 flies the camera home and re-enters the location. Over a window, the wheel stays that window's, so games and apps keep their scroll. Needs the pass-through plugin to see the wheel while the canvas is closed.

entry.name: DayTrail
entry.label: The plane remembers the day: the open canvas draws a faint fading line on the ground where the camera has travelled this session, the oldest part gone after about ten minutes. It lives in the zoomed-out world and stays out of the 1:1 seam, so the normal desktop never changes.

entry.name: HotRev
entry.label: The hot-reload revision, bumped by "make hot": each bump recompiles the scene tree (ui.qml) in the running session, so a look-polish edit lands without a re-login. The effect's logic lives in main.qml and still needs a compositor restart to change.

entry.name: CanvasHold
entry.label: The canvas modifier: mouse buttons (any of LeftButton, MiddleButton, RightButton, BackButton, ForwardButton, comma separated) that, held down for a moment anywhere on the normal desktop, make the location itself the canvas. A press shorter than a moment is the window's own click, so the button stays usable in games, browsers and every app that binds it; only a deliberate hold opens the canvas. While held, the desktop becomes the overworld at 1:1 - pixel for pixel, nothing visibly changes - and every canvas gesture works as if the overworld were open: the middle button grabs and navigates, a drag on a window moves it on the plane, the wheel zooms, a pointer parked at a screen edge keeps panning. Releasing applies the moves and closes again: hold, arrange, let go, done. Needs the kwin-canvas-passthrough plugin (or the plane-input shim) to see the press while the canvas is closed. BackButton (MB4, a mouse's side button) is the default.

entry.name: SwapButton
entry.label: Mouse buttons that, pressed while the canvas modifier is held, fly between the two most recent windows - an Alt-Tab on the plane: the camera springs to the other window, the focus follows, and releasing the modifier opens the location there, focused on it. ForwardButton (MB5, a mouse's side button) is the default, so the two side buttons are one hand on the plane.

entry.name: EdgePan
entry.label: While a pan button is held, or a window is in hand, a pointer within EdgePanMargin of a screen edge keeps panning that way until it leaves the band, the button is let go or the window is dropped. A dragged window rides the pan and stays under the pointer.

entry.name: EdgePanMargin
entry.label: Width of the edge band that starts edge panning, in screen pixels.

entry.name: EdgePanSpeed
entry.label: Edge panning speed in screen pixels per second at the very edge, tapering to nothing at the inner edge of the band.

entry.name: MouseFocusWindow
entry.label: Gesture on a window that applies with it focused: Click or DoubleClick, with optional Shift+, Ctrl+, Alt+, Meta+.

entry.name: FramesCarryWindows
entry.label: Dragging an activity's frames on the canvas carries that activity's windows with them, keeping their positions on screen. Off, the frames move over the windows.

entry.name: FocusTarget
entry.label: Where the viewport goes when a double-click on a window applies with it focused. "smart": the window comes wholly into view, and of the offsets that keep it so the one that leaves the most of the desk's other windows in view wins, so a window alone lands centred. "centre": the window's centre comes to the centre of the active screen, whatever that pushes off it. "window": the point clicked stays under the pointer at 1:1, unless that would leave the window hanging over an edge, in which case it is shifted the least it can be to fit. "desktop": a window inside a frame leaves the frame where it is; one outside every frame gets the frame centred on it, as "centre" does for every window. Every one of them moves the frames, their windows and the wallpaper together and writes nothing.

entry.name: MouseGotoActivity
entry.label: Gesture on an activity frame that applies with that activity current.

entry.name: MouseZoomToActivity
entry.label: Gesture on an activity frame that zooms the camera to that activity's frames (the toolbar swatches do this on a click).

entry.name: MouseSelect
entry.label: Gesture on a window that selects it alone.

entry.name: MouseSelectAdd
entry.label: Gesture on a window that adds it to the selection; its modifier plus a drag on the ground selects by rectangle.

entry.name: MouseSelectToggle
entry.label: Gesture on a window that toggles its selection.

entry.name: Palette
entry.label: Colour scheme for activities: default, okabe-ito (colour-blind safe), tol (colour-blind safe), ibm (colour-blind safe), mono (luminance steps only).

entry.name: SnapEdges
entry.label: Snap window and frame edges to other windows and frames while dragging.

entry.name: SnapCorners
entry.label: Snap corners to other corners while dragging.

entry.name: SnapGrid
entry.label: Snap positions to the canvas grid while dragging.

entry.name: SnapGridSize
entry.label: Grid step in canvas pixels for snap to grid.

entry.name: SnapDistance
entry.label: Snap when within this many screen pixels.

entry.name: MouseContextMenu
entry.label: Gesture on a window that opens the arrange menu for the selection.

entry.name: ArrangeGap
entry.label: Gap in canvas pixels between arranged windows.

entry.name: TidyGap
entry.label: Gap in canvas pixels between tidied windows, both between neighbours and between rows.

entry.name: MouseNewActivityAt
entry.label: Gesture on a window outside every frame that creates an activity centred on it.

entry.name: SwitcherAltShortcut
entry.label: The cluster switcher: this chord steps among the windows of the cluster the eye is on, fitted to that cluster instead of the whole plane - the quick switch among neighbours, where SwitcherShortcut sweeps everything. Hold the chord and tap it again to step, release it or press Enter to enter the chosen window, Esc to step back out. Bind this over KWin's own task switcher in System Settings.

entry.name: SwitcherSettleMs
entry.label: How long the switcher stays on the picked window after the chord's release before stepping in, in milliseconds. The pick settles under the eye for this beat, then the canvas enters by itself; tapping the chord again steps on, and Escape steps back out.

entry.name: SwitcherShortcut
entry.label: The switcher's chord: the hold's map as a toggle - the whole plane appears, Tab and Shift+Tab step the highlighted window, Enter enters it, Esc or the chord again steps back out. The window switcher the plane deserves; bind it over KWin's own Tabbox if you want it on Meta+Tab.

entry.name: ToggleShortcut
entry.label: Key sequence that steps out to the canvas and back in (enters the location under the screen centre).

entry.name: HomeShortcut
entry.label: Key sequence that returns to the canvas origin.

entry.name: PanLeftShortcut
entry.label: Key sequence that pans one step left at 1:1 (a slide), or moves the open canvas's camera. No default: every Meta+arrow chord is taken by KWin.

entry.name: Passthrough
entry.label: While the canvas is open, hand clicks, drags, the wheel and keys over windows to the real windows through the kwin-canvas-passthrough plugin when it is loaded. Title bars, edges, frames, tags and the toolbar stay the canvas's.

entry.name: PanStep
entry.label: One pan step as a fraction of the screen (0.05 to 1).

entry.name: PanDuration
entry.label: Length of the slide animation in milliseconds. 0 jumps.

entry.name: SceneFadeMs
entry.label: Length of the scene fade that masks a close from a zoomed-out overworld, in milliseconds. The seams at 1:1 are instant - the canvas and the desktop are the same picture there. A hidden knob, for measuring the transition.

entry.name: MovesGlide
entry.label: Every layout move plays: the tidy, the arrange, the send-to and the undo glide the windows to their new spots instead of teleporting them, and the commit hands the landed layout to the desktop. Off - the instant writes, for the physics-averse.

entry.name: QualityMode
entry.label: How much eye candy the canvas may run. Auto sheds it in steps as the system gets busy - reduced (the blur and the faint constellation go), minimal (no cluster web, no shadows, no z-depth) and bare (plain rectangles with names) - and puts it back when the machine breathes. The other settings hold that step always.

entry.name: CpuReduced
entry.label: The system's busy percentage at which Auto steps down to reduced fidelity. A hidden knob: the defaults are sensible, tune only if the ladder steps at the wrong moment.

entry.name: CpuMinimal
entry.label: The busy percentage at which Auto steps down to minimal fidelity. A hidden knob.

entry.name: CpuBare
entry.label: The busy percentage at which Auto steps down to the bare minimum. A hidden knob.

entry.name: GpuReduced
entry.label: The GPU's busy percentage at which Auto steps down to reduced fidelity. A hidden knob, alongside its CPU twin: whichever channel sees the worse pressure sets the step.

entry.name: GpuMinimal
entry.label: The GPU's busy percentage at which Auto steps down to minimal fidelity. A hidden knob.

entry.name: GpuBare
entry.label: The GPU's busy percentage at which Auto steps down to the bare minimum. A hidden knob.

entry.name: MemReduced
entry.label: The memory's used percentage at which Auto steps down to reduced fidelity. A hidden knob, alongside its CPU and GPU twins: whichever channel sees the worse pressure sets the step.

entry.name: MemMinimal
entry.label: The memory's used percentage at which Auto steps down to minimal fidelity. A hidden knob.

entry.name: MemBare
entry.label: The memory's used percentage at which Auto steps down to the bare minimum. A hidden knob.

entry.name: PanInertia
entry.label: A pan the hand lets go of keeps the plane moving, slowing by PanFriction, so a flick carries. A drag that pauses before the release, or a slow one, stops where it is put.

entry.name: PanFriction
entry.label: How quickly a flung pan slows, per second. 3 (the default) coasts about a third of the flick's own length further; higher stops sooner, lower carries further.

entry.name: SmoothZoom
entry.label: Wheel zoom and other camera moves spring to their destination, with the point under the cursor pinned, instead of jumping. Off, every camera move lands at once.

entry.name: CamSpring
entry.label: Camera spring rate in 1/s: how fast a smooth zoom or an animated camera arrives. 14 (the default) is about a third of a second, critically damped, so it does not overshoot; higher is snappier. Above 32 the spring's stepping becomes unstable, so the effective rate is capped there.

entry.name: WindowPhysics
entry.label: A dragged window carries weight: it lifts a little, trails and leans after the hand, and settles when it stops. Drawn only - the committed geometry is exact either way.

entry.name: PanSwipeFingers
entry.label: Touchpad swipe with this many fingers pans at 1:1, following the fingers. 0 turns it off. KWin's own three-finger swipes switch desktops and four-finger swipes open Overview; a matching count fires both.

entry.name: ActivityGap
entry.label: Gap in canvas pixels between the frame groups of neighbouring activities when first laid out.

entry.name: HiddenFrames
entry.label: Frames switched off from their tag, as "activityId|outputName". A hidden frame is not drawn and takes no windows.

entry.name: PinnedWindows
entry.label: Pinned windows, by caption. A pinned window is screen-fixed: it rides the camera and never leaves the screen - the one window that follows you everywhere on the plane, this model's "on all desktops". Drag it to move its spot; drag it past an edge and it bounces back into view.

entry.name: ClusterHomes
entry.label: The camera spots the clusters were left at, as JSON keyed by each cluster's members. A cluster is a room: the tour returns to the spot you left it at, and the digits jump straight there. A hidden knob, for persistence only.

entry.name: ClusterNames
entry.label: The names the clusters wear on their badges, as JSON keyed by each cluster's members. A hidden knob: the debug channel's "clustername" command sets a name.

entry.name: FollowActivation
entry.label: Pan the canvas so an activated off-screen window comes on screen.

entry.name: ClusterGap
entry.label: How near two windows must sit, in canvas pixels between their edges, to belong to the same cluster. Windows cluster automatically as they are dragged together, and part when they are dragged apart; the clusters are where the cluster travel keys fly between. 0 picks the size of the screen: a third of its smaller side.

entry.name: ClusterNextKey
entry.label: The key that flies the camera to the next cluster, in reading order on the plane.

entry.name: ClusterPrevKey
entry.label: The key that flies the camera to the previous cluster, in reading order on the plane.

entry.name: PublishGround
entry.label: Write the ground offset to the kwin-canvas-ground wallpaper via plasmashell.

entry.name: AutoActivate
entry.label: Open the canvas as soon as the effect loads (nested test harness).

entry.name: DebugCommand
entry.label: Command executed on reconfigure when DebugSeq changes (nested test harness).

entry.name: Verbose
entry.label: Write a trace of every decision the canvas takes to KWin's log, as [canvas] lines. Toggled live by the debug channel's "verbose" command.
